lessons.unit: Unit 1: My place in the world
lessons.title: My home, my school and my local area
objectives: Name places we can find in our local area
Say if something is natural or made by people
Say one way to look after our area

keywords.def: the streets and places close to where we live
made by nature, not by people, like a tree or a river
built or made by people, like a house or a road
a place where Muslims pray together

starter: Say Bismillah. Tell me one thing you can see from your window.
What is the name of the country we live in?
Is your home a house or a flat? Show me with your hands how big it is.

teach.heading: Where do we live?
bullets: We all live in a home.
Our home is in a street, a town or a city.
The streets and places near us are our local area.
teach.note: Start with Bismillah. Hold up a picture or drawing of a street. Ask: what is near your home? Take answers from children and write them on the screen. Keep it concrete: do not worry about names of towns, just near/far.

teach.heading: Places in a local area
bullets: Many areas have a shop, a park and a school.
Many areas have a masjid, a library and a bus stop.
Each place has a job. A shop sells things.
teach.note: Show 6 photos of typical UK places (shop, park, school, masjid, library, bus stop). For each, ask 'What do people do here?' Praise full sentences. Misconception: some children think the local area means only their own house.

teach.heading: Natural or made by people?
bullets: Natural things: trees, grass, rivers, hills.
Made by people: houses, roads, shops, bridges.
Allah created the natural world for us to look after.
teach.note: Play 'Natural / Made' on screen: show 8 pictures, children show thumbs up for natural and hands on head for made. A garden is a good tricky one: the plants are natural but the garden was planned by people. Accept either answer with a reason.

teach.heading: Looking after our area
bullets: We put litter in the bin.
We do not pick flowers in the park.
The Prophet (peace be upon him): cleanliness is half of faith (Sahih Muslim).
teach.note: Link care for the local area to adab. Ask: what could we do this week to keep our street clean? Note: you are citing the well-known hadith about cleanliness; keep it simple and say it plainly.

practice: Look at the picture of a street. Point to one natural thing and one man-made thing.
Tell your partner: 'In my area there is a ___.' Say it three different ways.
independent: Draw your home in the middle of a page. Draw and label three places near it.
Colour the natural things green and the man-made things blue in the picture sheet.
Stretch: add one thing that you would like in your local area and say why.
exit: Name one place in your local area.
Is a river natural or man-made?
lessons.homework: Walk or look around your street with an adult and draw or photograph two natural things and two man-made things.
lessons.send: Use real photos and word cards with pictures; allow children to point or draw answers. EAL: say each place name together and show the picture. Stretch: ask children to explain why a place is useful.

lessons.unit: Summer 1: The UK, its capitals and London (Bright Lights, Big City)
lessons.title: The four countries of the UK and their capitals
lessons.bigQuestion: What makes England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland one United Kingdom?
objectives: To understand that the United Kingdom is made of four countries, each with a capital city
successCriteria: All: name the four countries of the UK
Most: match each country to its capital city
Some: name a sea around the UK
lessons.crossCurricular: History: London is the setting for the Great Fire next week
lessons.smsc: Social: living together in four countries with different traditions

keywords.def: a land with its own name and people
the most important city of a country
England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland together
a big area of salty water
land with water all around it

hook.text: If you sailed all the way round Great Britain, which seas would you pass?

islamicLink.text: Allah tells us He made people into nations and tribes so that they may know one another (Al-Hujurat 49:13). The four countries of the UK have different places and ways, and we learn about them with respect.

starter.q: From space, the blue parts of Earth are:
A photo taken from high above is:

starter.a: For example: Europe, Asia or Africa

teach.heading: Four countries, one kingdom
bullets: England, Scotland, Wales, Northern Ireland
Together they are the United Kingdom
We say UK for short
teach.note: Show the UK map from the school's Our Wonderful World unit. Trace each country with the pointer.

teach.heading: Capital cities
bullets: England: London
Scotland: Edinburgh
Wales: Cardiff
Northern Ireland: Belfast
teach.note: A capital is the most important city. Say each pair together: England, London.

teach.heading: Seas all around
bullets: North Sea to the east
Irish Sea to the west
English Channel to the south
Atlantic Ocean to the north and west
teach.note: Great Britain is an island. Northern Ireland shares an island with Ireland.

teach.heading: Check
bullets: Vote in the Teams poll
teach.note: Share the results.

check.why: Cardiff is in Wales; Edinburgh is in Scotland and Belfast is in Northern Ireland.

practice.model:
London is a capital city.
It is in the biggest country, at the bottom of the map.
That country is England.

practice.q: Which sea is to the east of the UK?

independent.q: Core: On the blank UK map, write the four countries and their capitals.
independent.a: England: London; Scotland: Edinburgh; Wales: Cardiff; Northern Ireland: Belfast
independent.model: Teacher writes 'England' and 'London' first and draws a dot for London.

independent.q: Extend: Label two seas on the map.
independent.a: For example: North Sea and Irish Sea

independent.q: Stretch: Which country is the biggest?

exit.q: The UK has how many countries?
Big question: what makes the four countries one UK?
exit.a: They are joined together as one kingdom, with one government in London

lessons.homework: Make a UK map jigsaw: cut a printed map into the four countries and say each name and capital to your family.
lessons.send: SEND: map with the first letters given. EAL: country and capital cards with flags. Stretch: find the UK's longest river, the River Severn.

lessons.unit: Unit 1: My place in the world
lessons.title: Weather and the four seasons in the UK
objectives: Name the four seasons in order
Say what the weather is often like in autumn and winter

keywords.def: what the sky and air are like outside today
one of four parts of the year: spring, summer, autumn, winter
the season when leaves fall and days get shorter
how hot or cold it is

starter: Say Bismillah. Name the four countries of the UK.
What is the capital city of England?
What is the weather like outside today? Tell your partner.

teach.heading: What is weather?
bullets: Weather is what it is like outside.
It can be sunny, cloudy, rainy, windy, snowy or foggy.
Weather can change in one day.
teach.note: Show weather symbols one by one and ask children to act out each (shiver for cold, flap hands for wind). Ask: what did you wear today and why? This links weather to everyday life.

teach.heading: The four seasons
bullets: The year has four seasons.
They are spring, summer, autumn and winter.
They come round in the same order every year.
teach.note: Show a season wheel. Say the seasons in order and count on fingers. We are in autumn now (November). Ask: what is the next season? Many children will name a time such as Ramadan or Eid - gently bring them back to 'winter'.

teach.heading: Autumn and winter in the UK
bullets: In autumn leaves change colour and fall.
In winter it is cold. Days are short.
We wear coats, hats and scarves.
teach.note: Show photographs of the same park in each season. Ask: what is different? Encourage descriptive words (brown, bare, frosty). Mention that daylight is shorter in winter, so it gets dark early, which affects the times of prayer.

teach.heading: Spring and summer in the UK
bullets: In spring flowers grow and it gets warmer.
In summer it is warm and the days are long.
We wear T-shirts and sun hats.
teach.note: Link to the idea that the sun is higher in the sky in summer. Do not go into the reasons why seasons happen; just notice and describe. Ask who has a favourite season and why.

practice: Look at four photographs. Say which season each picture shows and how you know.
Choose the right clothes for a rainy autumn day. Explain your choice.
independent: Draw a picture of an autumn day. Add three weather or season words.
Cut and stick the four seasons in the right order.
Stretch: write one sentence about your favourite season.
exit: What is the weather often like in winter in the UK?
lessons.homework: Look outside for three days and draw the weather symbol for each day.
lessons.send: Give a word bank with pictures. EAL: practise weather words with actions. Stretch: ask children to compare summer and winter using the word 'but'.

lessons.unit: Unit 1: My place in the world
lessons.title: Making a simple map
objectives: Explain what a map is for
Use pictures and symbols to show places on a simple map
Make a simple map of the classroom or bedroom

keywords.def: a drawing of a place seen from above
a small picture or sign that stands for something
a box that explains what the symbols on a map mean
the way you go from one place to another

starter: Say Bismillah. Name the four seasons in order.
What are the four countries of the UK?
What is the weather like today? Show me with an action.

teach.heading: What is a map?
bullets: A map is a drawing of a place from above.
It helps us find places and find our way.
A map uses symbols, not full pictures.
teach.note: Show a bird's-eye photograph of a school next to a simple drawn map of the same school. Ask: what is the same and what is different? Introduce the idea that we look straight down from above. Hold a book flat and look down on it.

teach.heading: Symbols and a key
bullets: A symbol is a small sign for something real.
A tree can be a green circle. A road can be a grey line.
A key tells us what each symbol means.
teach.note: Build a simple key together on screen: green circle = tree, blue square = water, red square = house. Check understanding by asking what a blue square means. Misconception: children think symbols have to look exactly like the object.

teach.heading: A map of our room
bullets: Think of the room as seen from the ceiling.
Draw the door, the table and the window.
Use a symbol for each and make a key.
teach.note: Model drawing a map of your own classroom on the screen. Narrate each decision: where is the door? Is the table near the window? Use words such as next to, behind, in front. Let children tell you where to add things.

teach.heading: A route on a map
bullets: A route is the way from one place to another.
Use words: forward, left, right, turn.
Draw a line to show the route on the map.
teach.note: On your map, draw a route from the door to the window. Describe it with left and right. Left and right are tricky at this age: say 'my left hand has the ring' or hold up the L shape with the left hand.

practice: Look at a map of a park. Find the pond, the swings and the café using the key.
Say a route from the gate to the swings using forward, left, right.
independent: Draw a simple map of your bedroom or classroom from above.
Make a key with at least three symbols.
Stretch: draw a route from the door to your favourite place and describe it.
exit: What is a key on a map for?
Draw a symbol for a tree.
lessons.homework: Draw a map of the route from your bedroom to the kitchen. Add a key with two symbols.
lessons.send: Provide a printed outline of the room with spaces for symbols. EAL: label objects in two languages if helpful. Stretch: add a compass arrow showing north.

lessons.title: Earth from space
lessons.bigQuestion: What would you see if you looked down at the Earth from space?
objectives: To understand that pictures from space show the Earth's land, sea and clouds
successCriteria: All: point to the sea and the land on a picture of Earth
Most: find clouds and ice on a satellite image
Some: say that most of the Earth is covered by sea
lessons.crossCurricular: Science: the Moon and the Earth
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: awe at the earth seen from space

keywords.def: a picture of Earth taken from space
the dry ground we live on
a big area of salty water
white shapes in the sky made of tiny water drops
a view from high above

hook.text: From space, what colour do you think the Earth is? Why?

islamicLink.text: Allah made the earth for us to live on. Allah asks: 'Have We not made the earth a resting place?' (an-Naba' 78:6). From space we can see how much water Allah has given the earth, and we thank Him for it.

starter.q: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
Is the sea land or water?
Name the planet we live on.

teach.heading: The Earth from space
bullets: Astronauts took photos of Earth
It looks like a blue ball
Blue is sea; green and brown is land
teach.note: Show the 1972 'Blue Marble' photo taken from Apollo 17. Ask: what can you see?

teach.heading: Satellites
bullets: A satellite goes round the Earth
It takes pictures from space
We call them satellite images
teach.note: Show a satellite image of the UK. Point: sea, land, cloud.

teach.heading: White on the picture
bullets: Swirly white: clouds
White at the top and bottom: ice
Most of the Earth is sea
teach.note: The North and South Poles are covered in ice. Clouds move; ice stays.

teach.heading: Check
bullets: Vote in the Teams poll
teach.note: Share results.

check.q: On a picture of Earth from space, blue shows:
check.why: Blue is the sea. Land is green or brown and clouds are white.

practice.q: What colour is the sea on a satellite image?
practice.model:
Look at the picture.
Find the big blue areas.
Blue is the sea.

practice.q: Is there more land or more sea on Earth?

independent.q: Core: Colour a picture of Earth: blue for sea, green for land, white for clouds.
independent.a: Sea blue, land green, clouds white
independent.model: Teacher shows it first: blue all round the edges, green for the land shapes, white swirls on top.

independent.q: Extend: Point to the UK on the satellite image.
independent.a: The UK is in the sea to the north-west of Europe

independent.q: Stretch: Where is the ice on Earth?
independent.a: At the North and South Poles

exit.q: A picture of Earth from space is called a:
Big question: what would you see if you looked down at the Earth from space?
exit.a: Blue sea, green and brown land, white clouds and ice

lessons.homework: With an adult, look at your home area on a free online map in satellite view and find a field, a road and some water.
lessons.send: SEND: a printed satellite image with blue, green and white dots to match. EAL: sea, land, cloud with pictures. Stretch: find a river on the satellite image.

lessons.unit: Summer 1: The UK, its capitals and London (Bright Lights, Big City)
lessons.title: London landmarks from the air
lessons.bigQuestion: How can you find a landmark when you look down from the sky?
objectives: To understand how aerial photographs show London's landmarks from above
successCriteria: Most: match a landmark to its aerial photo
Some: say how the River Thames helps us find places
lessons.crossCurricular: Maths: shapes we can see from above (circles, rectangles)
lessons.smsc: Cultural: famous places in our capital city

keywords.def: a building or place that is easy to spot
a photo taken from high above
the river that flows through London
something that crosses a river
a drawing of a place from above

hook.text: If you flew over London in a helicopter, what would you look for first?

starter.q: The UK has how many countries?
Name the capital of Northern Ireland.

teach.heading: London's landmarks
bullets: Tower Bridge crosses the Thames
The London Eye is a big wheel
St Paul's Cathedral has a dome
Big Ben is a bell in a clock tower
teach.note: Show a photo of each from the ground first. These are buildings, not people.

teach.heading: Looking down from above
bullets: An aerial photo is taken from high up
Roofs look like shapes
Roads look like lines
teach.note: Compare the ground photo of Tower Bridge with an aerial photo of it.

teach.heading: Use the river
bullets: Find the River Thames first
It bends like a ribbon
Landmarks sit near the river
teach.note: Model: find the Thames, follow it, spot Tower Bridge crossing it.

model.problem: Find Tower Bridge on the aerial photo
steps: Look for a bridge with two towers

teach.heading: Check
bullets: Vote in the Teams poll
teach.note: Share the results.

check.why: Aerial means from the air, so the camera is high above.

practice.q: What crosses the river: a bridge or a dome?
practice.model:
A river is water.
To cross it we need something to walk or drive on.
That is a bridge.

practice.q: Which landmark is a big wheel?

independent.q: Core: Match four ground photos to their aerial photos on the sheet.
independent.a: Tower Bridge, London Eye, St Paul's Cathedral, Big Ben's tower matched
independent.model: Teacher matches Tower Bridge first: two towers, crossing the river.

independent.q: Extend: Draw the River Thames and put Tower Bridge on it.
independent.a: A wavy river line with a bridge across it

independent.q: Stretch: Why is a river a good clue on a map?
independent.a: It is long and easy to see, so you can follow it

exit.q: Big question: how do you find a landmark from the sky?
exit.a: Look for big shapes and clues like the river, then match them

lessons.homework: With an adult, look at your own street on an online map from above and find one landmark.
lessons.send: SEND: two photos to match, not four. EAL: landmark word cards with pictures. Stretch: find Buckingham Palace on the aerial photo.

lessons.unit: Summer 1: The UK, its capitals and London (Bright Lights, Big City)
lessons.title: My area and central London
lessons.bigQuestion: Is the place where you live more like a city, a town or a village?
objectives: To understand how my home area is similar to and different from central London
successCriteria: All: sort features into human and physical
Most: tally features seen from a window
Some: say one way my area differs from London
lessons.crossCurricular: Maths: tally marks and counting in fives
lessons.smsc: Social: belonging to our local community

keywords.def: something people made, like a road
something nature made, like a hill
a very big place with lots of buildings
a small place with few houses
marks we make to count things

hook.text: What can you see from your window that you could also see in the middle of London?

teach.heading: Human and physical
bullets: Human: roads, houses, shops, mosques
Physical: rivers, hills, trees, sea
teach.note: Made by people or made by nature? Allah created the physical features.

teach.heading: Central London
bullets: Very tall buildings
Lots of buses, roads and people
The River Thames
teach.note: Show an aerial photo of central London.

teach.heading: A window survey
bullets: Look out of a window
Make a tally mark for each feature
Count the marks
teach.note: Model with a photo from a window: three houses, one tree, one road.

teach.heading: Check
bullets: Vote in the Teams poll
teach.note: Share the results.

check.why: A hill is made by nature; roads and shops are made by people.

practice.q: Is a river human or physical?
practice.model:
Did people make the river?
No, it is part of nature.
So it is physical.

practice.q: Is a bus stop human or physical?

independent.q: Core: Do a window survey. Tally houses, trees, roads, cars and shops, then circle the biggest number.
independent.a: A tally chart from the pupil's own window with totals
independent.model: Teacher shows the tally from the class photo first.

independent.q: Extend: Write one way your area is like London and one way it is different.
independent.a: For example: both have roads; London has much taller buildings

independent.q: Stretch: Is your area a city, a town or a village? Why?
independent.a: Answer with a reason about size and number of buildings

exit.q: Big question: is your area a city, a town or a village?
exit.a: Any answer with a reason, compared with London

lessons.homework: Do the window survey again at a different time of day. Did the number of cars change?
lessons.send: SEND: picture tally chart with five features. EAL: human and physical picture cards. Stretch: add a sixth feature of your own.
